spec.description:
Legacy cancel-replace: edits the parameters of a live order by cancelling it and creating a new order with the adjusted parameters, returning a new `txid`. Superseded by `AmendOrder`, which edits in place and resolves this endpoint's caveats with better performance. Caveats: triggered stop-loss/take-profit orders are not supported; orders with a conditional close attached are not supported; an edit reducing volume below the already-executed volume is rejected; `cl_ord_id` is not supported; executions stay associated with the original order rather than the replacement; queue position is not maintained.

**API Key Permissions Required:** `Orders and trades - Create & modify orders` and `Orders and trades - Cancel & close orders`

request.title: EditOrderRequest
request.description: Parameters for cancel-replacing a live order.

userref.description: An optional user-specified integer id associated with this edit request. Note: the parent order's `userref` is not retained on the new order after the edit.

txid.description: The original order's transaction ID (txid), or its user reference (userref) if unique to a single order -- if the userref matches multiple orders, the edit is denied with an error.

volume.description: Order quantity in terms of the base asset.

displayvol.description: For `iceberg` orders only, the quantity to show in the book while the rest of the order quantity remains hidden. Minimum value is 1/15 of `volume`.

asset_class.description: Required on requests for non-crypto pairs, e.g. `tokenized_asset` for xstocks.

price.description: Limit price for `limit`/`iceberg` orders, or trigger price for `stop-loss`, `stop-loss-limit`, `take-profit`, `take-profit-limit`, `trailing-stop` and `trailing-stop-limit` orders. Either `price` or `price2` may be prefixed with `+`/`-` (offset from last traded price) or `#` (add or subtract depending on order direction/type), and suffixed with `%` for a relative percentage instead of an absolute difference. Trailing stops must use the `+` prefix, and also accept the `%` suffix.

price2.description: Secondary price for `stop-loss-limit`, `take-profit-limit` and `trailing-stop-limit` orders. For trailing stops this is a relative offset (`+`/`-` prefix, optionally `%` suffix) from the trigger price to the limit price -- `+0` sets the limit price equal to the trigger price.

oflags.description: Comma-delimited list of order flags. Only `post` (post-only, available when `ordertype = limit`) can be changed on edit -- every other flag from the parent order is retained, and `post` itself must be explicitly re-supplied on the edit request or it is dropped.

deadline.description: RFC3339 timestamp (e.g. `2021-04-01T00:18:45Z`) after which the matching engine should reject this edit if it is still queued due to latency, minimum now()+2s, maximum now()+60s.

cancel_response.description: If true, the client receives a pending-replace acknowledgement before the order is fully replaced.

validate.description: If true, the edit is validated only and never reaches the matching engine.

response.title: OrderEditedFrame
response.description: Wire frame; the generated method returns `result`.

error.description: Wire envelope field; see the core.

txid.description: New transaction ID, present if the order was successfully replaced.

descr.title: OrderDescription
descr.description: Human-readable description of the replacement order.

orders_cancelled.description: Number of orders cancelled by this edit -- either 0 or 1.

newuserref.description: The `userref` passed with this edit request, if any.

error_message.description: Error message, present if the edit was unsuccessful.

notes: `nonce` is dropped from the request body -- transport-injected by the client core (authed_request), never a caller-supplied parameter.
`txid` converted from upstream's `oneOf: [string, integer]` to `anyOf` per spec-authoring rule 4.
`oflags` has no declared `type` upstream (a schema gap) -- filled in as `string` since its description and every sibling `oflags` field elsewhere in this subsection are comma-delimited strings.

`status` is described as 'Status of the order: Ok or Err' but upstream's own example shows lowercase `"ok"`, disagreeing on casing -- left as a bare string rather than guessing an enum casing, per spec-authoring rule 2.
This endpoint is legacy (superseded by AmendOrder per upstream's own description) but still live; left `unverified` unset per the brief.

Deliberately left as a flat request body (production_standards.md S12), not a `requestBody`/`anyOf` discriminated union like `add_order`/`add_order_batch`: unlike those, an edit-by-id request carries no `ordertype`/`order_type` field at all to discriminate on -- the edit targets an existing order by `txid`, and Kraken's wire contract for this endpoint provides no local field whose value would select which variant's required-field profile applies. Building an `anyOf` here would mean inventing a discriminant the venue doesn't provide, which authoring rule 2's "never invent" bar rules out just as much for a discriminant as for an enum value.
